title: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil
claimed_value: Broad Windows utility covering tweaks, fixes, updates, and debloat that could surface safe missing deltas for computa's Windows tuning catalog.
current_overlap: audited 2026-09-03: all 67 tweaks payload-mapped; 8 absorbed, 13 documented-noop, ~40 rejected, 3 watchlist — see parity/winutil-parity-table.md
evidence_needed: Field-by-field diff between WinUtil tweak catalog and computa debloat_tweaks.yaml
Proof that any imported deltas are reversible and honestly verifiable
Evidence that the imported changes help performance, privacy, or maintenance without scope creep
risk_notes: WinUtil is broader than computa and includes non-gaming maintenance scope
Do not import app install/update orchestration unless product scope expands deliberately
Avoid bundling one-click tweak packs without per-setting evidence
proposed_shape: Add only missing reversible debloat/privacy/service entries as explicit computa tweaks; keep package-management and general Windows toolbox scope out.
next_action: Done. Re-audit only on major WinUtil catalog changes; SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB stays on the watchlist pending a RAM-aware handler feature.

title: AtlasOS
claimed_value: Aggressive Windows optimization and privacy project that may contain reversible per-setting ideas worth benchmarking for gaming profiles.
current_overlap: partial — computa already has game-specific profiles, power tuning, and debloat, but not a whole-OS image-style optimization lane.
evidence_needed: Separation of reversible per-setting deltas from image/install-time modifications
Benchmark proof on computa target games and display paths
Rollback-safe implementation path for every kept delta
risk_notes: Direct wholesale import conflicts with computa's reversible transaction model
Atlas-style system-wide image assumptions are a meaningful scope expansion
Many claims in this category are anecdotal until measured on target hardware
proposed_shape: Treat AtlasOS as a source of candidate deltas only; reject wholesale preset or image-style adoption.
next_action: Extract a shortlist of reversible AtlasOS deltas and tag every non-reversible or image-only change as out of scope.

title: O&O ShutUp10++
claimed_value: Large privacy and telemetry toggle catalog that can be compared against computa's existing tier-1 and tier-2 debloat coverage.
current_overlap: partial — computa already ships privacy and telemetry tweaks plus service controls, but no explicit ShutUp10 parity or rationale doc.
evidence_needed: Mapping of ShutUp10 toggles to existing or missing computa settings
Verification that any missing toggles fit computa's restore and safety guarantees
Clear explanation of which privacy tweaks are placebo, harmful, or out of scope
risk_notes: Privacy toggle suites often mix safe telemetry reductions with feature-breaking options
A big matrix without guidance becomes cargo-cult tweaking
Some settings may be organization-policy or edition-dependent
proposed_shape: Create an explicit privacy-toggle mapping doc and import only the deltas that fit computa's evidence and rollback bar.
next_action: Draft a ShutUp10 parity table against debloat_tweaks.yaml and mark each row as covered, missing, rejected, or watchlist.

title: NVCleanstall
claimed_value: Lean NVIDIA driver installation path that could reduce driver bloat around gaming setups.
current_overlap: adjacent but absent — computa already has NPI and planned NVAPI read/merge work, but it does not currently mediate driver installation.
evidence_needed: Explicit product-scope decision on whether driver installation belongs inside computa
Rollback and recovery story for any driver-package mutation path
Proof that the benefit is meaningful beyond what current NPI/NVAPI surfaces already cover
risk_notes: Driver install mediation is much higher risk than profile tuning
Bad rollback here can strand the machine rather than just revert a profile
This can easily become an installer/distribution project instead of a tuning project
proposed_shape: Do not build install automation first; decide the scope boundary and document it before any implementation work.
next_action: Write a scope decision note: either keep NVCleanstall out of computa or define a narrowly optional offline-safe preparation lane.

title: Winaero Tweaker
claimed_value: Broad catalog of Windows registry and shell tweaks that may surface a few reversible quality-of-life or gaming-adjacent settings.
current_overlap: partial — computa already handles many targeted Windows changes, but it does not yet document which Winaero-class tweaks are intentionally excluded.
evidence_needed: Identification of any gaming-relevant reversible deltas
Proof that a kept tweak changes user outcomes rather than just surface preferences
Explicit rejection reasons for cosmetic or non-verifiable registry tweaks
risk_notes: This tool's breadth makes scope drift likely
Many tweaks here are cosmetic or folklore-driven rather than performance-backed
User-facing polish tweaks should not be confused with gaming optimization
proposed_shape: Harvest only a tiny number of measured, reversible settings and document the rest as intentionally out of scope.
next_action: Split Winaero-class tweaks into performance-relevant, UX-only, and reject buckets before any code proposal.
